Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint because my Victoria 's Secret store card was closed. When I called to inquire about the reason for the closure, the representative informed me that it was closed due to inactivity. I asked if she could reopen my account, to which she responded that she would not be able to do so without pulling my credit again. Therefore, according to CFR Part 1026.11 ( 2 ) ( B ) states : " Nothing in paragraph ( b ) ( 1 ) of this section prohibits a creditor from terminating an account that is inactive for three or more consecutive months. An account is inactive for purposes of this paragraph if no credit has been extended ( such as by purchase, cash advance, or balance transfer ) and if the account has no outstanding balance. '' This implies that they should not have closed my account due to inactivity. Additionally, by informing me of the closure, they are still selling my security, which was generated when I filled out the application, as applications can be transferred to third parties. This process securitizes the application, allowing them to sell it on both primary and secondary markets. 
12 CFR Part 1002.2 Definitions 12 CFR Part 1002.2 ( A ) Account - means an extension of credit. When employed in relation to an account, the word use refers only to open-end credit. 12 CFR Part 1002.2 ( F ) Application - means an oral or written request for an extension of credit that is made in accordance with procedures used by a creditor for the type of credit requested. The term application does not include the use of an account or line of credit to obtain an amount of credit that is within a previously established credit limit. A completed application means an application in connection with which a creditor has received all the information that the creditor regularly obtains and considers in evaluating applications for the amount and type of credit requested ( including, but not limited to, credit reports, any additional information requested from the applicant, and any approvals or reports by governmental agencies or other persons that are necessary to guarantee, insure, or provide security for the credit or collateral ). The creditor shall exercise reasonable diligence in obtaining such information.

( c ) Authority to Decline or Rescind ( 1 ) In general. A consumer reporting agency may decline to block, or may rescind any block, of information relating to a consumer under this section, if the consumer reporting agency reasonably determines that -- ( A ) the information was blocked in error or a block was requested by the consumer in error ; ( B ) the information was blocked, or a block was requested by the consumer, on the basis of a material misrepresentation of fact by the consumer relevant to the request to block ; or ( C ) the consumer obtained possession of goods, services, or money as a result of the blocked transaction or transactions.

To Whom It May  Concern, 15 U.S. Code 1692F Unfair Practices A debt collector may not use unfair or unconscionable means to collect or attempt to collect any debt. Without limiting the general application of the foregoing, the following conduct is a violation of this section : ( 1 ) The collection of any amount ( including any interest, fee, charge, or expense incidental to the principal obligation ) unless such amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law. 
( 2 ) The acceptance by a debt collector from any person of a check or other payment instrument postdated by more than five days unless such person is notified in writing of the debt collectors intent to deposit such check or instrument not more than ten nor less than three business days prior to such deposit. 
( 3 ) The solicitation by a debt collector of any postdated check or other postdated payment instrument for the purpose of threatening or instituting criminal prosecution.

If they can not provide proof, I demand justice. 3-203. TRANSFER OF INSTRUMENT ; RIGHTS ACQUIRED BY TRANSFER. Primary tabs ( a ) An instrument is transferred when it is delivered by a person other than its issuer for the purpose of giving to the person receiving delivery the right to enforce the instrument. ( b ) Transfer of an instrument, whether or not the transfer is a negotiation, vests in the transferee any right of the transferor to enforce the instrument, including any right as a holder in due course, but the transferee can not acquire rights of a holder in due course by a transfer, directly or indirectly, from a holder in due course if the transferee engaged in fraud or illegality affecting the instrument. ( c ) Unless otherwise agreed, if an instrument is transferred for value and the transferee does not become a holder because of lack of indorsement by the transferor, the transferee has a specifically enforceable right to the unqualified indorsement of the transferor, but negotiation of the instrument does not occur until the indorsement is made. ( d ) If a transferor purports to transfer less than the entire instrument, negotiation of the instrument does not occur. The transferee obtains no rights under this Article and has only the rights of a partial assignee.

Law 15 U.S.C. 1681-1681x states The Act ( Title VI of the Consumer Credit Protection Act ) protects information collected by consumer reporting agencies such as credit bureaus, medical information companies and tenant screening services. Information in a consumer report can not be provided to anyone who does not have a purpose specified in the Act. Companies that provide information to consumer reporting agencies also have specific legal obligations, including the duty to investigate disputed information. In addition, users of the information for credit, insurance, or employment purposes must notify the consumer when an adverse action is taken on the basis of such reports. The Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act added many provisions to this Act primarily relating to record accuracy and identity theft. The Dodd-Frank Act transferred to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau most of the rulemaking responsibilities added to this Act by the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act and the Credit CARD Act, but the Commission retains all its enforcement authority. 


All furnishers must have in place reasonable procedures to respond to notifications from CRAs that information furnished is the result of identity theft, and to prevent refurnishing the information in the future. A furnisher may not furnish information that a consumer has identified as resulting from identity theft unless the furnisher subsequently knows or is informed by the consumer that the information is correct. Section 623 ( a ) ( 6 ). If a furnisher learns that it has furnished inaccurate information due to identity theft, it must notify each consumer reporting agency of the correct information and must thereafter report only complete and accurate information. Section 623 ( a ) ( 2 ). When any furnisher of information is notified pursuant to the procedures set forth in Section 605B that a debt has resulted from identity theft, the furnisher may not sell, transfer, or place for collection the debt except in certain limited circumstances. Section 615 ( f ).

Notice of Federal Law Violations Your email communication asserting that I owe an alleged debt constitutes a violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692b ( 2 ). Your use of symbols, branding, and/or logos within that communication constitutes a further violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692b ( 5 ).

Absent my prior express consent or authorization from a court of competent jurisdiction, your attempt to contact me constitutes a violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692c ( a ). Your conduct further constitutes harassment and abuse in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692d ( 2 ). You also employed false, deceptive, and misleading means to attempt collection in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 6 ) ( B ) by implying a legally enforceable obligation without lawful authority.

Radius Global Solutions has further used and compelled the disclosure of my Social Security number, in violation of 42 U.S.C. 408 ( a ) ( 8 ). As a result, you are liable for damages pursuant to 18 U.S.C. 3571 ( c ) ( 3 ) and 15 U.S.C. 1692k ( a ) ( 2 ), including statutory, actual, punitive damages, and damages for emotional and mental distress.

Strict Liability Facts, Not Legal Conclusions The United States Supreme Court has made clear that the FDCPA is a strict liability statute. In Jerman v. Carlisle, McNellie, Rini, Kramer & Ulrich LPA, 559 U.S. 573 ( 2010 ), the Court held that debt collectors are liable for FDCPA violations regardless of intent.

The violations identified herein are not conclusions of law, characterizations, or speculative assertions. They are statements of fact, established directly by the contents, form, and transmission of your companys email correspondence sent to me. Your own communication constitutes the operative evidence giving rise to liability. No inference, assumption, or legal embellishment is required.

Accordingly, any claim of mistake, ignorance, clerical error, or lack of intent is legally irrelevant and factually immaterial.

No Standing / No Enforceable Rights Under settled principles of contract law, including 17 Am. Jur. 2d 125126, a party lacking privity, consideration, and participation in the original contract can not enforce that contract absent a valid, provable assignment. You have produced none.

Further, billing statements alone do not constitute competent evidence of ownership, standing, or the amount allegedly owed. As established in Hinkle v. Midland Credit Management, absent authenticated account-level documentation and a complete chain of title, the alleged debt is legally unenforceable.

Your claimed authority is therefore rejected.

An unbroken chain of title from origination to present 3. Proof of consideration exchanged for each transfer 4. The original contract or agreement governing the account 7. All Pooling and Servicing Agreements ( PSA ) and trust documents showing whether the account was securitized or sold into a trust 8. The complete account transaction history 9. Legal proof of ownership Refusal to Pay/ Demand for Waiver / Cease and Desist I refuse to remit payment on the alleged obligation. In regard to the EFTA ( Electronic Funds Transfer Act ) and EFT ( Electronic Funds Transfer ) : When I use a payroll advance, the repayment is in the form of an Electronic Funds Transfer. My direct deposit paycheck is immediately taken ( seized ) and applied to my outstanding payroll advance. As explained below, this is in direct violation of the Electronic Funds Transfer Act, Regulation E. My money is taken when I some amount of time to repay it. I could have 30 or 40 days left to pay my advance back to the bank. This often leaves my account at a {$0.00} balance. There are often overdraft fees associated with my account, when I technically have use of the payroll advanced funds for usually 30 to 40 days. This is for all Fifth Third Bank customers stuck in this payroll advance circle. If customers were allowed the entire 45 days, it would assist them in getting out of this situation. I believe these payroll advance products are predatory due to the facts I 've listed above and are not intended to help the customer, but trap them. 
A violation occurs when your are forced to sign away your legal rights provided by EFTA to obtain a payroll advance. A violation of the Electronic Funds Transfer Act, Regulation E occurs when the bank makes it a condition for an extension of credit that repayment will be by means of preauthorized EFT. This is disallowed except for credit extended under an overdraft credit plan or extended to maintain a specified minimum balance in the consumer 's account. See excerpt of the EFTA below. 
VI. Other RequirementsPreauthorized Transfers-Section 205.10Compulsory use. The financial institution may not make it a condition for an extension of credit that repayment will be by means of preauthorized EFT, except for credit extended under an overdraft credit plan or extended to maintain a specified minimum balance in the consumer 's account. ( Section 205.10 ( e ) ( 1 ) ). The financial institution may offer a reduced APR or other cost related incentive for an automatic payment feature as long as the creditor offers other loan programsfor the type of credit involved. It requires debt collectors to follow certain procedures when communicating with consumers about debt collection : Validation notice Within five days of the initial communication, debt collectors must send consumers a written notice that includes the amount of the debt, the creditor 's name, and a statement that the debt will be considered valid if the consumer doesn't dispute it within 30 days. The notice must also state that the debt collector will provide the consumer with the original creditor 's name and address if requested within 30 days. 
Disputed debts If the consumer disputes the debt, the debt collector must stop collection efforts and : Obtain verification of the debt or a copy of a judgment Mail the verification or judgment to the consumer Other provisions Debt collectors are also prohibited from taking certain actions, such as : Threatening or taking non-judicial action to disable or dispossess property if there is no right to possession, no intention to take possession, or the property is exempt by law Using unfair or unconscionable means to collect a debt, such as collecting amounts that aren't authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law

As per 12 U.S.C. 1431, the powers and duties of banks in credit transactions involving natural persons for personal, family, or household purposes must adhere to certain standards. It is crucial to emphasize that the term " consumer '' in credit transactions characterizes such transactions when the party involved is a natural person, and the transaction 's subject is primarily for personal, family, or household purposes.

Additionally, the terms " open end credit plan '' and " open end consumer credit plan '' as defined in 15 U.S.C. 1602 encompass plans where the creditor reasonably anticipates repeated transactions, prescribes the terms of such transactions, and includes provisions for a finance charge computed periodically on the outstanding unpaid balance. It is essential to note that even if credit information is verified intermittently, the transaction remains an open end credit plan or open end consumer credit plan. 
The term creditor means any person who offers or extends credit creating a debt or to whom a debt is owed, but such term does not include any person to the extent that he receives an assignment or transfer of a debt in default solely for the purpose of facilitating collection of such debt for another.

Consumer complaint narrative:
CFPB Complaint Narrative ( Deceptive and Misleading Practices ) Product type : Home equity / mortgage related financial product Company : Point ( home.point.com ) Complaint Summary I am reporting what I believe to be deceptive and misleading practices related to consent, disclosures, and representations on the website home.point.com.

The website presents consent language stating that by clicking Continue or View my offer, the consumer agrees to be contacted by the company regarding product offerings and agrees to multiple policies, including cellular phone contact, electronic communications, electronic signatures, and privacy terms. This consent appears to be bundled and mandatory in order to proceed, without a clear or meaningful opportunity to decline marketing contact while still accessing required disclosures. 

The presentation creates a coercive click-through scenario where marketing contact consent is effectively required to move forward. This undermines informed consent and may mislead consumers into believing the consent is limited to necessary disclosures rather than ongoing product solicitations.

Additionally, the site prominently states that Prequalification will not impact your credit score, without providing sufficient clarity regarding what consumer data is accessed, how it is used, or whether soft credit inquiries or alternative consumer reports are involved. The lack of transparency may mislead consumers regarding the scope of data collection and credit reporting implications.

The overall design, wording, and placement of disclosures appear intended to minimize consumer understanding and discourage meaningful review or refusal of consent, which may violate consumer protection standards regarding clear, conspicuous, and non-deceptive disclosures.

I am requesting that the CFPB review this companys consent practices, representations, and disclosure design for compliance with federal consumer financial protection laws.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I was approved for a mortgage loan with Zillow Home Loans , LLC for the purchase of a property. The loan had passed underwriting, and I signed my closing documents, including the Promissory Note and Deed of Trust, on XX/XX/year>. 

When signing, I included a lawful reservation of rights annotation on the Note stating All Rights Reserved, Without Prejudice, which is a recognized method under the Uniform Commercial Code and common law for preserving legal and equitable rights in a negotiable instrument. This reservation did not alter the financial terms or substantive obligations of the loan in any way.

Following my execution of the documents, Zillow informed me that they would not fund the loan unless I re-signed the Note and Deed of Trust without any additional protective language. They stated that unless I removed the lawful reservation of rights, they could not submit the loan to investors such as XXXX XXXX. 

This was an ultimatum that placed me in a position where I was required to waive a lawful right in order to receive funding. I declined to waive my rights, and as a direct result, Zillow canceled my loan. I received an official adverse action notice stating that the sole reason for denial was : " BORROWER REFUSED EXACT SIGNATURE REQUIREMENTS '' Why This Violates ECOA : The ECOA ( Pub. L. 93-495, 88 Stat. 1500, 701 ( a ) ) prohibits a creditor from discriminating against an applicant because the applicant has exercised any right under the Consumer Credit Protection Act. My annotation was an exercise of such a right the preservation of legal and equitable interests in my own promissory note, a negotiable instrument under law. Zillows cancellation of my loan solely for exercising this right constitutes an adverse action prohibited by ECOA. 

Additional Legal Concerns : Breach of Contract : Zillow had approved my loan and was contractually obligated to fund at closing. Their refusal to perform unless I waived my rights is a breach of the financing agreement.

Coercion : Conditioning funding on the surrender of a lawful right is a form of coercion that violates fair lending standards.

Constructive Conversion : By taking possession of my signed promissory note and refusing to fund, Zillow retained an asset of value without performing its side of the transaction.

And we could avoid foreclosure. However, all combined debts exceeded the value of the property, therefore the Estate decided to short sell the property.

They have used tactics that have prevented me from selling the property in order to proceed to foreclose on the property. For example, when evaluating the propertys value they have used the same appraiser for several years who values the property with vastly different numbers from one report to the next. However, he never manages to report values that are anything competitive to the surrounding properties. In fact, no property in the local area has ever sold for the value that PHH has placed on this property, which has been vacant for several years and is smaller than most in the surrounding area. There are thousands of qualified licensed appraisers but PHH only sends the same person to the property to inflate the value of the property and make it difficult for me to sell it on the open market and settle the foreclosure. 

Next, they continue to require excessive amounts of paperwork after they have scheduled an auction. When I think we have concluded our loss mitigation application, and I am only waiting on final documents, they send me scrambling for additional paperwork, delaying already scheduled closings. Once they receive the paperwork as requested then they stop communicating with my representatives, sometimes for several weeks as an auction sale approaches. Messages go un-responded to and this has been an ongoing pattern for more than a year. While we wait on final short sale approval documents, in the meantime, their foreclosing attorney will reschedule an auction sale at the same time. 

Once we submit all documents and secure a buyer they stop communicating for weeks waiting for a scheduled auction sale to be executed after we have worked diligently to settle. They make false promises of providing the final documents to us to close, when in truth, they are waiting for the house to be sold at auction after I have completed all their requests and worked hard to settle the estate debts.

I have had several auction sales scheduled that I had to beg a judge to stop or file bankruptcy to try and settle the matter. I have been granted several stays by judges just to have repeated delays from PHH, which puts me back in the same situation. PHH continues to give me the run around. Their foreclosing attorney goes after the family estate while the mortgage servicer allows me to believe we are in settlement negotiations. I am dealing with multiple entities, and they are being disingenuous the entire time about their intentions. All I want to do is sell the property for the true value and settle all the outstanding estate debts that are linked to this property. I have paid numerous 3rd parties to help me and I keep trying to settle this foreclosure while they keep trying to auction the property. They are disingenuous and have not acted fairly in their dealings.

They promised to provide a final short sale approval and then they turned around and said THEIR OWN appraisal had expired that they failed to reorder. They denied my application and proceeded to move forward to an auction sale. After another auction sale was stayed by me, they reordered the same appraiser to come back and he concluded the home have jumped $ XXXX in values within a few months by using comps sold across town and neglecting all the ones sold on the same block.

The stated reason for denial of both Special Forbearance and Repayment Plan was : Your loan is less than 61 days delinquent.

This loan is VA-guaranteed, which UWM has confirmed. Under the VA Servicer Handbook ( M26-4, Chapter 5 ), there is no requirement that a loan be 61 days delinquent to approve Special Forbearance or a Repayment Plan. VA guidance explicitly allows approval before 61 days delinquent. The denial therefore applied non-VA, conventional criteria to a VA-backed loan.

Their inability to provide this information violates 12 C.F.R. 1024.36 ( Request for Information ) and demonstrates a lack of continuity of contact under 1024.40.

The denial letter also fails 1024.41 ( d ) of Regulation X, which requires the servicer to state the specific reason for denial and, if applicable, the owner/assignee and its rule. However, I have recently reviewed my credit reports and discovered that the Affirm account is either not reported at all or is only reported to one credit bureau, which results in an incomplete and inconsistent credit profile. Despite multiple inquiries to Affirms customer service, I have not received any resolution or clarification regarding their reporting practices. 

Applicable Laws and Consumer Rights Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), the following provisions are relevant : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) : Furnishers of credit information, such as Affirm, have a duty to provide accurate and complete information to credit reporting agencies if they choose to furnish data.

15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) : Consumer reporting agencies must follow reasonable procedures to ensure the maximum possible accuracy of the information contained in credit reports.

15 U.S.C. 1681n and 1681o : Establish civil liability for willful or negligent noncompliance with the FCRA.

While the FCRA does not require furnishers to report to all bureaus, if they do choose to report, they are obligated to do so accurately, consistently, and in good faith. Failure to report in a timely and complete manner across bureaus may misrepresent a consumers creditworthiness and limit access to financial opportunities.

Company : InComm / Vanilla Visa Product : Prepaid Gift Card ( Vanilla Visa ) I am filing a complaint regarding an unauthorized fraudulent transaction on a Vanilla Visa prepaid gift card.

I am requesting : A secondary review or escalation of this fraud case Consideration of a goodwill reimbursement Transparency regarding the merchant that processed the fraudulent transaction I am not disputing that time limits exist, but I am requesting a fair review based on the facts of unauthorized use and the reasonable inability to detect the fraud earlier.

Pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( if applicable ), and my rights under Georgia law, I hereby request that you provide, in writing, the following : 1. A copy of the pre-sale Notice of Disposition sent to me.

2. A copy of the post-sale accounting, including the sale date and sale price.

3. An itemized statement of how you calculated the alleged {$14000.00} balance.

Until you provide this information, you must cease all collection activity. Any further reporting of this debt to credit reporting agencies without proper verification will be disputed as inaccurate under the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

If you can not produce the required notices and documentation, I demand that you cease all collection efforts and request immediate removal of this account from all credit reporting agencies.

Under federal law I absolutely have the right to raise legal grounds to dispute a charge-off under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and possibly contract or debt collection laws if : The underlying debt was paid in full, and The creditor still reported a charge-off What Is a Charge-Off? 

A charge-off is when a creditor marks a debt as unlikely to be collected ( usually after 180 days of non-payment ). It is : Reported as a serious derogatory mark on your credit Still collectible ( doesnt mean the debt disappears ) Often sold to collections or pursued through legal means When Is It Not Lawful to Report a Charge-Off?

A charge-off would be inappropriate or unlawful if : 1. The Debt Was Paid in Full If the creditor received payment in full, it is not permitted to report the account as a charge-off They may report it as Paid in Full or Closed Paid as Agreed Under the FCRA ( 15 USC 1681s-2 ), I can send a written dispute to the furnisher ( creditor ) directly. They must : Investigate Correct the information if its inaccurate If they fail to correct it, I will and can file a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ). Which has been done twice now already!!! If theres financial harm to my credit ; which there is, I will be filing a claim under the FCRA or FDCPA.
